title: Neovim Cheatsheet
subtitle: Complete nvim command reference - searchable, fast, always free
description: A fast, searchable Neovim cheatsheet covering every essential nvim command: modes, navigation, editing, text objects, search & replace, splits, tabs, buffers, macros, LSP, and more.

legend.label: Normal
legend.tip: The default mode - you're here unless you've switched. Navigate, run operators, and issue commands. Enter with Esc from any other mode. Most commands only work in Normal mode.

legend.label: Insert
legend.tip: Type text directly into the buffer. Enter with i (before cursor), a (after), o (new line below), or O (new line above). Return to Normal with Esc or Ctrl+[.

legend.label: Visual
legend.tip: Select text interactively, then apply an operator. Enter with v (character), V (line), or Ctrl+v (block). Apply d, c, y, >, < to the selection - returns to Normal automatically.

legend.label: Command
legend.tip: Type Ex commands starting with :, or search with / and ?. Enter with : from Normal mode. Run with Enter, cancel with Esc. Supports tab completion for commands, files, and options.

cards.title: Neovim-Specific
cards.tip: Features unique to Neovim or its ecosystem. LSP keymaps (grr, gri, grn, gra, etc.) are built-in defaults, no config needed, working on any machine or server (K hover and ]d/[d diagnostics since 0.10; the gr* family since 0.11). Note: gd is a built-in Vim motion (local declaration), not an LSP default. Plugin managers like Lazy.nvim and Mason require installation.

items.tip: Run Neovim's built-in health checks for plugins and system dependencies. Shows what LSP servers, tools, and providers are properly installed.
Open a built-in terminal emulator inside a new buffer. The terminal runs in a special mode - normal editing keys are passed to the shell, not Neovim.
Exit terminal mode back to Normal mode. By default Esc is sent to the shell rather than Neovim, so this two-key chord is the standard way out (you can remap Esc to trigger it).
Open the Lazy.nvim plugin manager UI to install, update, or remove plugins. Lazy.nvim is the most popular Neovim plugin manager - requires it to be configured in your init.lua first.

Open Mason to browse and install external tools - LSP servers, DAP debug adapters, linters, and formatters. Mason manages the binaries; you still configure each LSP server in your init.lua via lspconfig or similar.

Show hover documentation for the symbol under the cursor. Built-in default since Neovim 0.10 - no config needed. Requires an LSP server attached to the buffer. Press K again to enter the hover window.

Built-in Vim motion: jump to the local declaration (first occurrence) of the keyword under the cursor in the current function or file. This is NOT LSP go-to-definition, which has no default mapping; map vim.lsp.buf.definition() yourself, or use Ctrl+] for a tag jump. Ctrl+o jumps back.
Show all references to the symbol under the cursor in a quickfix list. Built-in default since Neovim 0.11, grr (two r's) not gr. Use :cn / :cp to navigate the quickfix list.
Jump to the implementation(s) of the symbol under the cursor, useful for interfaces and abstract methods. Built-in default since Neovim 0.11, no config needed.
Rename the symbol under the cursor across the entire project via LSP. Built-in default since Neovim 0.11, smarter than find-and-replace because it understands scope and references.

Trigger a code action at the cursor: auto-import, extract variable, fix diagnostic, etc. Also works in Visual mode on the selection. Built-in default since Neovim 0.11. You may have seen <leader>ca used instead, that is a custom mapping for the same thing, not a built-in.
List all symbols in the current file (functions, classes, variables) via LSP. Built-in default, no config needed. Results open in the location-list, use :lnext / :lprev to navigate.
Show the function signature (parameter types and docs) for the call under the cursor. Built-in default since Neovim 0.11, works in Insert mode while typing a function call.
Jump to the next (]d) or previous ([d) diagnostic in the buffer - errors, warnings, and hints (from any source, not only LSP). Built-in defaults since Neovim 0.10, no config needed.
Format the current buffer using the attached LSP server
Show the diagnostic error/warning under the cursor in a floating window
